literal: Graciousness those-who-lack eyes they-lack; eyes those-who-possess graciousness even-the-lack is-not.
translation: Those who lack graciousness do not truly have eyes. For those who truly possess eyes, there is no lack of graciousness.
modern: கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாதவர்கள் கண்களை உடையவர்கள் அல்லர். உண்மையான கண்களை உடையவர்களிடம் கண்ணோட்டம் இல்லாமல் இருப்பதில்லை.
explanation: This couplet equates the physical possession of eyes with the moral quality of graciousness or compassionate consideration (கண்ணோட்டம்). The poet states that people who lack this graciousness are effectively blind, as their eyes do not serve their true human purpose. Conversely, those who truly possess eyes will never be found lacking in graciousness. The repetition of the word 'கண்' (eye) emphasizes that true vision is not merely physical sight, but the ability to look upon others with kindness.
